texts.preamble: Sulabh Sharma @ Amar Chaubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 June, 2025 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:13121 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 23 rd Of June, 2025 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 10 of 2024 Sulabh Sharma @ Amar Chaubey Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance: Mr. Ankur Maheshwari - Advocate for the appellant. Mr. Sanjay Singh Kushwaha - Govt. Advocate for the resp Judgment
texts.facts: This miscellaneous second appeal has been filed under Section 71 (6) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, arising out of order dated 06.08.2024 passed by Principal District and Sessions Judge / Appellate Tribunal, Food Safety and Standard Act, Guna in Criminal Appeal No.413/2022, as well as the order dated 19.07.2022 passed by the Adjudicating Officer (Food Safety) / Additional District Magistrate, Guna in Case No. 55/S-147/2021-22. 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in short, are that a complaint was filed by Food Security Officer to the effect that a search party went to the Namkeen factory belonging to the appellant on 20.11.2020. The factory premises was found to be locked. Upon enquiry, it was found that the appellant is the owner of the factory in the name and style of "Choubey Food Product". Multiple telephonic calls were made to the appellant, but he did not open the lock of the factory and, accordingly, under the orders of the S.D.M., the lock of the factory was broken open. The search team along with S.D.M. carried out the inspection of the factory premises. Finished products in the names of Laxmi NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13121 2 MSA-10-2024 Namkeen, Navrang Namkeen, which were sealed in packets, raw materials used for preparing namkeen like maida, besan, Oil, red-chilli Powder, packets of salt, poha, spices etc. were found in the factory premises which appeared to be of sub- standard quality. The utensils for manufacturing of namkeen and machines for packing namkeen were also found. Cooking range / stove (bhatti), which is made Sulabh Sharma @ Amar Chaubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107945799/ 1 of clay/brick, was also found. In the factory, no packing in the name of Choubey Food Product was found. Wrappers of Laxmi Namkeen, Navrang Namkeen, Siddharth Namkeen, Diamond Namkeen, etc., were found and it appeared that an attempt is being made to cheat the general customers. Accordingly, under the orders of the S.D.M., samples of Laxmi Namkeen, and Navrang Namkeen, which were packed in pouch, were collected, and maida, besan, oil, red-chilli powder, salt, poha, which were lying in open condition, were also collected and the empty wrappers were seized. Thirteen bags of Maida, 25 bags of Namkeen, 15 kgs of Besan, 10 kgs of Poha, 10 kgs of Chilli Powder, 50 kgs of salt, 5 litres of edible oil, as well as the factory premises, were sealed. Panchanama was prepared and the signatures of the panchas were obtained. The memorandum in form No. 6 was prepared in accordance with law and the second copy of form No. 6 was kept separately in a sealed envelope. All ten seized samples were sent along with form No. 6 to the Food Analyst, State Food Examination Laboratory, Bhopal. The report dated 05.01.2021 was received from the laboratory. The samples of namkeen packed in Laxmi Namkeen, Navrang Namkeen were found to be misbranded, and edible oil was found to be unsafe. Accordingly, complaint was filed before the Adjudicating Officer (Food Safety) / Additional District Magistrate, Guna and Case No. 55/S-147/2021-22 was registered. It is not out of place to mention here that an FIR was also lodged against NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13121 3 MSA-10-2024 Amar Choubey - appellant. Notice of the complaint was issued to the appellant. Appellant submitted his reply and claimed that as per the provisions of Article 20 (2) of the Constitution of India, no one can be punished twice for the similar offence, and also claimed that Section 300 of Cr.P.C. also provides for the similar provisions. The evidence of Ravi Shivhare, Food Security Officer, and Naveen Jain were recorded. Being aggrieved by the said order, the appellant preferred an appeal, which too has been dismissed by the appellate Court. 3. Challenging the order passed by the Courts below, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that since an FIR under Sections 272, and 273 of IPC was lodged, and appellant was also detained under the National Security Act, therefore, appellant cannot be punished twice for the similar offence. It is further submitted that the procedure prescribed for collection and seizure of samples was not followed.
